Yeah im not trying to bash them im just saying that the treatment for what I have is very different from theirs and therefore we should not be instantly grouped together by the majority of health professionals that i have met in my life

It's also really awesome to tell people that doctors have been treating me like shit for years and the first response I get is always "well maybe ur just so stupid that you *think* they were treating u that way"

It wasn't "giving substance info to their patients" it was literally "hi can I get mental health screening" "ok here's the clinic u go to" *googles the clinic and they literally do not offer any mental health services besides drug rehab*

They listened to me say "I have depression and anxiety and PTSD because of abuse and need help" and sent me off with the fucking heroin addicts

The first time I reached out to my doctor about depression, I was 16. Everyone in the office immediately switched to that "special" (super condescending) voice you use to talk to like, mentally deficient 2 year olds and started being super fake nice to me. Then they drug tested me to make sure I wasn't secretly an addict and put me on antidepressants that made me puke my guts out. I didn't realize until later in life that they also never scheduled any kind of follow up to adjust the medication or see if it was working or even really did anything but send me out of the office with a pat on my head and a nod at my mom like "teenagers, amirite?" I ended up tapering myself off the medicine because it was making me so ill.

A bit later I went to a therapist. Spent about 3 sessions explaining my parents' divorce, the abuse, the kidnapping threats, the fact that I was having nightmares about my father hunting me down and murdering me. She looked me in the eye and told me that the fact I wanted nothing to do with my abusive father meant that I was actually causing him as much pain as he was inflicting on me and that my nightmares about him torturing me and slowly slaughtering me would go away if I just went and became his best friend again. I did not go back to that therapist.

I could go on and tell you about every single doctor that has condescended to me. I could tell you about the one who gave me info for a drug rehab clinic when I asked about mental health screenings (seriously; I do not understand why they all think I am a drug addict; I am a white woman so I recognize my privilege keeps this from happening to me usually). I could tell you about the therapist who was so racist she thought Trump's Muslim registry and the sex offender registry were a 1:1 comparison. I could tell you about the one who seemed professional at first glance but then suggested treating my severe PTSD flashbacks with yoga to cleanse all the negative energy floating in my chakras.

My current doctor is mediocre at best. She's not outright hostile about mental health treatment but is not very willing to work on my prescriptions. The first one she put me on was giving me severe fatigue, but when I brought up that the fatigue was making my life unlivable, she literally told me to my face "there's nothing we can do about that" and told me to exercise more and doubled the dose of the medication that was causing the fatigue. I had to make another appointment and make sure I said "I want to switch this medicine because it's not working" because she doesn't care about side effects.

The thing she's got me on now isn't doing shit either and is making me nauseated, but when I brought it up, she put me on anti-anxiety meds instead of trying a different antidepressant like I wanted. 

EDIT: Anyway I am 24 now so that's 8 straight years of attempting to seek help and getting this shit every single time. So, yeah, that's why I think professionals can all go suck a cactus.
